intro_paras: One family per block: what the code does, read from the code, and what changed between revisions. Written by an LLM session, each sentence tied to the one revision it was read from - a family whose file has changed since is marked stale. This is a description, not a measurement, and it decides nothing.

The Date column is three different facts, each named: in the name is a date the author or the generator wrote into the class name, site is the published site's post date for the files taken from it, and repo is the last commit that touched the file in the repository it was harvested from - which is the revision's date where the repository has its own history and the date of an import where it does not (repo, import, when 90 % of a repository's files share one commit date). No date here is the moment an author published a strategy unless the column says so. Dates are read from evidence/SOURCE_DATES.json; what is missing stays missing.

families.name: Zaratustra
families.idea_html:
One comparison decides everything: while RSI(7) sits above RSI(14) the strategy is long, while it sits below it is short, and each side is closed as soon as the two cross back. There is no other filter and no signal-per-candle logic - the position is a state of the RSI spread. Exits in practice come from the risk settings, which are deliberately tight: 1% stoploss, 0.1% trailing stop and a flat 1% take-profit.

Caveat: The site's own family table advertises this family as 10x with a trailing stop. This revision's leverage() returns 1, so the published description and the code in the corpus disagree about position size - the description there may belong to a different revision or to a bot configuration.

families.name: Slope
families.idea_html: A pure swing-point reversal: scipy.signal.argrelextrema marks the local minima and maxima of the close over a rolling 64-bar window, a fresh local minimum opens a long and a fresh local maximum closes it, with the short side mirrored. There is no stoploss and no profit target in the usual sense - stoploss -0.999 and minimal_roi 1 mean the trade only ends when the opposite extreme appears.

V3 is the largest revision (143 lines) and moves ROI, stoploss and the trailing offset again; V4 removes the protections() block; V5 arms the trailing stop at a 1% offset; V6 adds a minus_di condition and raises the offset to 6.5%.

families.name: EMA + Fibonacci
families.idea_html: Perfect trend alignment on Fibonacci-length EMAs: EMA(34/55/89/144/233) of the typical price, and the long requires the +DI series of the same lengths stacked in ascending order (34>55>89>144>233) with the last one above -DI; the short mirrors it on the -DI side. The exit throws the trade out on any cross of the price with the 233 EMA, so the strategy rides an aligned trend but leaves as soon as price loses the longest average. The 0.99 stoploss is nominal - the exit signal is the real risk control.

families.name: Rsiqui
families.idea_html: The trigger is the slope of an EMA-smoothed RSI, not the RSI level alone: long when RSI is below the entry level and the smoothed RSI gradient turns up, short when RSI is above the upper level and the gradient turns down; each side closes when the gradient turns against it and RSI has crossed the exit level. It is a mean-reversion scalp at 5m with hyperopt-driven thresholds (entry 30-70) and a steep ROI ladder (22% decaying to 0 after ~110 minutes) over a 27% stoploss.

families.name: GnF
families.idea_html: A synthetic greed/fear index decides the direction: momentum (close against SMA20), volatility (NATR14) and a volume sentiment (up-volume minus down-volume) are each min-max normalised over a 20-bar window and averaged into one 0-1 number. Above 0.7 the strategy is long, below 0.3 short, and a trade is only opened while volume exceeds its own 50-bar mean; the opposite threshold closes the side, so the index crossing the band is what turns the position.

families.name: E0V1E
families.idea_html:
A 5m scalper whose entry is a bundle of conditions ORed together rather than one rule: EMA(8/16) against EMA/SMA(15) and RSI(4/14/20), the stochastic-fast fastk, and a Bollinger band around the typical price are collected into a list and reduced with `lambda x, y: x | y`, so any single member can open a trade. The exit side is where the work sits: a custom_stoploss that locks in above 1% profit and treats trades tagged 'ewo' differently, plus a custom_exit that reads the fastk and RSI columns of the current candle. minimal_roi and the 0.99 stoploss are nominal next to that.

Caveat: The custom_stoploss branches on the entry tag (`if 'ewo' in enter_tags`), so the same file holds two different exit rules depending on which condition opened the trade - a reader who evaluates only the stoploss number will read the risk wrong.

families.name: Ichimoku
families.idea_html:
The Ichimoku cloud used as a filter around a Tenkan/Kijun cross rather than as the signal itself: the long needs the Tenkan line to cross above the Kijun line while the cloud is red, and the short is not the mirror but a different rule. Later revisions keep the same cross and read the cloud from a higher timeframe through informative_pairs, or replace the candle with its Heikin-Ashi version and compare that against the daily Senkou A/B - so the family is one idea read against different chart types.

Caveat: The entry in the strategy read here buys a Tenkan/Kijun cross while `cloud_red` is true, i.e. while the cloud is bearish - the opposite of the textbook reading, where a cross is only taken in the direction of the cloud. Its `populate_sell_trend` also assigns an empty tuple, so exits in this revision come from minimal_roi alone.

families.name: NostalgiaForInfinityX
families.idea_html:
The X line is a trading system rather than a signal: an entry built from a long list of indexed conditions, a custom_exit of several hundred lines, adjust_trade_position for DCA and a set of _bad_trade_controller_* handlers that decide when a losing trade gets de-risked, held or closed. The numbered strategies are one line of work: each iteration adds a candlestick-pattern filter to a VWAP/EMA/RSI/ATR frame, until roger27 trades `bullish_conditions | candlestick_patterns & macd_condition` and stops the trade on peak-profit drawdown. families.name: VWAPStrategy
families.idea_html:
A VWAP band system: for every candle the code asks whether the body touched the daily VWAP from below, from above or both, stores that as a state column, and then asks the RSI(16) to sit below its own 10th percentile (or the mirror, above the 90th) while the close is outside the Bollinger band - so the trade needs a VWAP event, an RSI extreme and a band break at once, joined with reduce(lambda x, y: x & y, conditions). The stop is a custom_stoploss that is rewritten in almost every strategy of the family; the entry is not.

Caveat: These strategies are numbered by the harvest, and the numbers do not order them: VWAPStrategy_11 has stoploss -0.1, _12 has -0.2 and drops the trailing stop, and the undecorated strategy has -0.07 again. The table below lists variants, not a history.

families.name: ClucHAnix
families.idea_html:
The 'Cluc' band entry taken over from the CombinedBinHAndCluc family, but computed on Heikin-Ashi candles and filtered by a 1h ROCR: the buy needs rocr_1h above a threshold and the band event (lower band above zero, a band distance and a body above their thresholds, a lower wick smaller than a fraction of the distance) on the Heikin-Ashi close, and the sell uses a Fisher transform. Caveat: This stem is the base of three families on this page - ClucHAnix, ClucHAnixV* and ClucHAnix_5m - and the CombinedBinHAndCluc line uses the same band event without the Heikin-Ashi wrapper. They are not code-identical, so no duplicate verdict covers them, but they share one entry rule.

families.name: bbrsi
families.idea_html:
Two lines of code carry the idea: buy when the RSI is above 25 while the close is below the lower Bollinger band at one standard deviation, sell when the RSI is above 95 while the close is above the one-sigma upper band. The RSI threshold works as a filter in the opposite direction to the usual reading - it rules out the deepest falls - and the two bands are plotted at one and four standard deviations, so the entry and the exit use different widths.

Caveat: This stem, BBRSI and BbandRsi are the same idea under three spellings and three cases, which is why the ranking counts them as three of the largest families. The RSI level also changes between strategies (25 here, 33 in BBRSI3366), so the threshold is part of the tuning, not of the design.

families.name: BBMod
families.idea_html:
